activeSession.task: Redesigned the Glossaire module (M7) end-to-end: Phase 1 audit → Phase 2 plan → backend (aggregates, reactivate, create-time duplicate check) → frontend (concept-first registry + TermWorkspace + form). Audit found the module was still using the generic DataTable (same header-hover issue fixed in Traductions) and two real backend gaps: reactivate was completely unimplemented at every layer (no way to undo a deactivation from the UI), and creerTerme had no duplicate check even though importerTermes (CSV import) already did. Fixed both, plus added GET /glossaire/aggregates for real KPI counts. Built glossary.adapters.ts (GlossaryConceptViewModel/TermVariant/getPrimaryVariant/toApiPayload) so the UI never touches termeFr/termeEn directly — a frontend multilingual-ready layer with zero backend migration, per the brief's explicit constraint. Confirmed (by diff review, no changes made) that the Traductions module's actual glossary-suggestion code path (traductionsApi.suggestions → getSuggestionsGlossaire, inside the traduction module) is untouched; also confirmed glossaireApi.suggestions/suggererTermes is dead code, never called by the client. Live-validated all three backend additions against the real dev DB via a disposable scratch script (deleted after use). Then did the usual close-out: doc-sync (TASKS.md, changelog.md, quick-ref.md, project/overview.md, project/architecture.md, manifest.json) and a Notion backlog update per explicit user request, expanding the existing 'glossaire import UI' backlog item into a broader recommendation — multiple import sources (CSV/Excel, document-based extraction), each needing its own dedicated UI surface, not just a backend endpoint.
